chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

Al-Tayyar said to him, and I was present, 'This, which is increased, is it from the Masjid?' So he said: 'Yes, they have not yet reached the remoteness of the Masjid of Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them).'

key_terms.الطَّيَّار: Al-Tayyar (a narrator, often identified as Muhammad ibn al-Tayyar)
key_terms.زِيدَ: Increased/added (referring to the expansion of the mosque)
key_terms.صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا: The prayers/blessings of God upon them two
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَ إِسْمَاعِيلَ: The Masjid of Ibrahim and Ismail (referring to the original or foundational structure of the Kaaba/Masjid al-Haram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the expansion of the Sacred Masjid in relation to the station of Ibrahim and Ismail?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the dynamic nature of the Sacred Mosque's boundaries, confirming that the 'added' areas are fully integrated into the sanctity of Al-Masjid al-Haram. The Imam clarifies that the current construction has not yet reached the Station of Ibrahim (Maqam Ibrahim) and the area of Ismail, indicating that the mosque's spiritual and legal status extends beyond the original foundation built by the Prophets. This underscores the principle that expansions to the Haram are not merely structural but carry the same merit as the original sacred space.
